questions.s:
A student follows the rate of reaction between marble chips, CaCO3 and dilute hydrochloric acid.
CaCO3 + 2HCl → CaCl2 + CO2 + H2O
Which set-ups show the apparatus that are suitable for this experiment?

A student sets up the apparatus as shown below to collect a sample of clean, dry gas X.
Which row correctly gives the identity of gas X and drying agent?
o: gas X: ammonia; drying agent: calcium oxide
gas X: ammonia; drying agent: concentrated sulfuric acid
gas X: hydrogen chloride; drying agent: calcium oxide
gas X: hydrogen chloride; drying agent: concentrated sulfuric acid

questions.s: Which sequence of procedures is used to separate a pure, dry sample of hydrated copper(II) sulfate, CuSO<sub>4</sub>.5H<sub>2</sub>O, from a mixture containing hydrated copper(II) sulfate and calcium carbonate, CaCO<sub>3</sub>?
o: distillation → crystallisation → heating to remove all water
fractional distillation → filtration → heating to remove all water

questions.s:
A paper chromatography experiment is used to find the Rf value for Fe2+(aq). The chromatogram is shown.
To make the spot containing Fe2+(aq) more visible, the paper is sprayed with a locating agent that forms a precipitate of iron(III) hydroxide on the spot.
In the chromatogram, the Rf of Fe2+(aq) is given by ……….(1)………. and the colour of the precipitate is ………(2)……….

A liquid is suspected to be pure ethanol.
What is the best way to test its purity?

The graph shows the change in the temperature of a substance with time when it is heated from −10 °C to 60 °C.
Which statement describes the change taking place between the points?
o: Energy is released from points P to Q.
Kinetic energy of the particles remains constant from points P to U.
Particles gain energy to weaken the forces of attraction from points S to T.
There is a large increase in the volume of the substances from points R to S.

questions.s:
The number of valence electrons for elements hydrogen to magnesium was plotted against the proton number of the element.
Which graph was obtained?

A beam of protons was passed through an electrostatic field between two charged plates. The electrostatic field deflected the beam of protons towards the negatively charged plates. The lower the relative mass of the particle, the larger the deflection.
The experiment was repeated using a beam of electrons in place of the beam of protons.
Which row correctly shows the extent of deflection and the direction of the beam of electrons?
o: extent: deflected less than beam of protons; direction: opposite direction to beam of protons
extent: deflected less than beam of protons; direction: same direction as beam of protons
extent: deflected more than beam of protons; direction: opposite direction to beam of protons
extent: deflected more than beam of protons; direction: same direction as beam of protons

questions.s:
An atom of element X is represented by 94X.
Which statement about an atom of X is correct?
o: It is in Group 14 of the Periodic Table.
It is in Period 4 of the Periodic Table.
It forms an ion with a 2+ charge.
The total number of protons and neutrons is 13.

questions.s:
Naturally-occurring bromine has a relative atomic mass of 80 and consists entirely of two isotopes of relative atomic masses 79 and 81.
What can be deduced about naturally-occurring bromine from this information only?
o: Bromine contains the two isotopes in equal proportions.
Bromine has different number of electrons.
Bromine isotopes have different number of protons.

questions.s: Which substance contains both ionic and covalent bonds?

• has a high melting point;
• is a good conductor of electricity;
• is malleable.
What could Y be?

questions.s:
0.24 g of an element, X, is reacted with 240 cm3 Cl2 to form a chloride with the formula XCl2 at r.t.p.
What is element X?

The manufacture of nitric acid, HNO3, involves 2 steps.
Step 1: 2NO + O2 → 2NO2
Step 2: 4NO2 + 2H2O + O2 → 4HNO3
What is the maximum number of moles of nitric acid that could be formed from 0.50 moles of nitrogen monoxide, NO?
Which hydrocarbon has the highest percentage of hydrogen by mass?

On heating, ammonium nitrate, NH4NO3, decomposes to form dinitrogen oxide and water.
NH4NO3 → N2O + 2H2O
When 100 g of an impure sample of ammonium nitrate is heated, 30 g of water is formed.
What is the percentage purity of ammonium nitrate in the sample?

A student titrates 25.00 cm3 of 0.100 mol/dm3 of sulfuric acid with 0.250 mol/dm3 of sodium hydroxide using a methyl orange indicator.
H2SO4(aq) + 2NaOH(aq) → Na2SO4(aq) + 2H2O(l)
She records the volume of sodium hydroxide used to be 24.00 cm3.
Which statement(s) is/are correct?
1 The colour of the solution at the end of the titration is yellow.
2 The colour of the solution at the end of the titration is orange.
3 She has exceeded the end-point of the titration.
4 She has just reached the end-point of the titration.
Which of the following oxides can react with aqueous potassium hydroxide?

When an excess of lead(II) carbonate reacts with dilute sulfuric acid, the reaction stops after only a small amount of gas has been given off.
Which statement best explain why this happens?
o: An insoluble layer of lead(II) sulfate is formed on lead(II) carbonate.
The concentration of acid decreases rapidly.

titration: potassium nitrate; metal + acid: zinc sulfate; metal carbonate + acid: copper(II) sulfate; precipitation: silver chloride

questions.s:
Industrial ammonia is obtained by the Haber process.
N2(g) + 3H2(g) ⇌ 2NH3(g) ∆H = −92 kJ / mol
Which statement is incorrect about the process?
o: The industrial catalyst used is finely divided iron.
The reaction is endothermic, hence a temperature of 450 °C is used.
The hydrogen needed is obtained mainly by cracking of petroleum oil.
250 atm favours the production of ammonia but is difficult to maintain.

questions.s:

The amount of light that passes through the test-tube was plotted against the volume of sodium hydroxide solution added.
What is X?

Disproportionation is a reaction in which the same element is oxidised and reduced simultaneously.
Which reaction is an example of disproportionation?

gasobservations
Xcolourless solution of potassium iodide turns brown
Ypurple acidified potassium manganate(VII) turns colourless

o: gas X: oxidising agent; gas Y: oxidising agent
gas X: oxidising agent; gas Y: reducing agent
gas X: reducing agent; gas Y: oxidising agent
gas X: reducing agent; gas Y: reducing agent

questions.s:
The table gives statements about the properties between an electrolytic cell and a simple cell.
In which row are both statements correct?
o: electrolytic cell: converts chemical energy to electrical energy; simple cell: converts electrical energy to chemical energy
electrolytic cell: movement of positive and negative ions across electrolyte; simple cell: flow of electrons from reactive metal to less reactive metal
electrolytic cell: reduction takes place at positive electrode; simple cell: oxidation takes place at positive electrode
electrolytic cell: electrolyte decomposes to form new substances; simple cell: positive electrode dissolves

questions.s:
In an electrolysis experiment, the same amount of charge deposited 38.4 g of copper and 14.4 g of titanium. The charge on the copper ion is 2+ and titanium has a relative atomic mass of 48.
What was the charge on the titanium ion?

Four elements identified only as W, X, Y and Z are all found in the third period of the Periodic Table. W, X, Y and Z are not the actual chemical symbols of the elements.
1 W does not lose, gain or share electrons with other elements.
2 X forms an alkaline solution when reacted with cold water.
3 Y is diatomic.
4 X and Z forms ions which are smaller than their atoms.
Using the information provided, what is the most likely order of arrangement of these elements from left to right in the third period?
Which diagram correctly shows the conditions necessary for the rusting of iron and also the metal that can be used to prevent rusting by sacrificial protection?
Which metal carbonate is most likely to melt but not decompose upon heating?

The diagram shows part of the carbon cycle. P, Q and R refer to specific processes of the carbon cycle.
Which row correctly describe the energy changes of these processes?
o: P: endothermic; Q: exothermic; R: endothermic
P: endothermic; Q: exothermic; R: exothermic
P: exothermic; Q: endothermic; R: endothermic
P: exothermic; Q: endothermic; R: exothermic
